description: CGDIS is Luxembourg's national fire and rescue service, which also runs the 112 emergency call centre and coordinates emergency medical responses. Its statistics page gives headline figures for each year and links to annual activity reports for 2018 to 2025. In 2025 the services carried out 75,814 interventions, fought 2,665 fires, made 1,539 first responder and 10,507 SAMU emergency medical interventions, and the 112 centre handled 258,036 emergency calls, with 89 per cent of interventions being rescue to persons. Reports for 2018 to 2024 give the same headline figures for earlier years. Coverage is national. The reports are free and available to download as PDF or read as web versions; no licence terms are stated. Caveats: statistics are published as report figures, not open data tables, and categories change as the service, created in 2018, has evolved. Simulation uses: calibrating national demand for fire, rescue and emergency medical responses, sizing call centre capacity, and comparing Luxembourg with neighbouring systems. Related records: the German fire service statistics (data-dfv-german-fire-service-statistics) and the CTIF world fire statistics (data-ctif-world-fire-statistics) provide comparisons.
